body: Ultimately having those as svg files and using some react-svg-loader (or smg) would be easier. It adds noise to the code currently. Let's keep that in mind for later. I am not sure this is easy/compatible with babel webpack loader plugin that we need to use.

Yes, we could provide two utility method 👍 
- an erase merge 
- a combined merge 

In the meantime, updating the docs is fine.

I use storybook mainly because of issues in the doc side conf and I wanted to move on. Also it guaranteed me that it was a complete isolated env and it's quite fast when you want to do a lot of little experiments/variations. 

But I believe once those issues will be solved, we will have the same things with our widgets demo pages. I push it because I want you to have a look at the default styling but It was not intended to last. 

As for storybook, it's still under development so they add some nice stuff regularly like snapshoting for free this week. But for now I don't believe it could feet nicely within our doc. For example Airbnb add it as a complete external website (http://airbnb.io/react-dates)

body: Isn't that possible with a simple transition?

Saying that the default theme as a key root bind to classname A and the user theme as a key root bind to classname B.
If you perform an erase merge root will be bind to classname B. 
If you perform a combined merge, root will be bind to classname A and B. 

Maybe not the better name though :)
You mean in the test file having a createURL function a little be smarter than this : createURL={() => '#'} ?
